Accuracy and fairness are closed: Marcus, Dreyfus, AMI Labs, the equal-size export-control tags and the 'year or two behind' correction all hold on their sheets. Two ids the ledger marks fixed are not. ch15-s06 still has a pinned, captioned Hassabis beat (confirmed on the sheet and at source line ~151). ch10-s12 re-added the compute ratio as 'one-seventh … GNMT+RL (derived)', which slipped past the '1/7' check. Both are re-routed with tighter absent checks. The ch15-s05 settlement label is ruled final as 'ANTHROPIC · $1.5B SETTLEMENT · PIRATED BOOKS'. The work that will move the gate is sound: an L1505 gain envelope plus an m19 re-fit so 'to plan' clears the music, a slower solo L0114 retake (the user's wording is kept), and stamp foley for ch15-s08 and ch14-s07. For visual: idle poses for the cast (including Hinton's hair), ghost-text discipline in the kit, and four placeholder or composite frames. For story: a legible ch15-s08 stamp, the ch15-s05 opening that names the labs, a verdict slip before the final stamp, and the Versailles callback in L1502. dimensionNotes.accuracy: Every quote matches its source word for word, every claim id exists, and contested claims are shown as contested, with Anthropic's own settlement named on screen. What keeps it from a 9: one callback line ('China trailing by years?') no longer matches its corrected candle, and the narrator's pronunciation of real names has not been checked by a person.
dimensionNotes.depth: AlexNet and the transformer are both worked through step by step with real numbers (a 3x3 edge stencil, the 12M-vs-60M overfitting scale, a hand-computed softmax over 'river bank'), and an expert can check every value. Each era's belief has a named dissenter and a duration.
dimensionNotes.clarity: Most of the film is picture first, symbol second, so a newcomer can follow it. It is held back by a few unspoken jargon captions ('one-seventh the compute of GNMT+RL', 'untrained toy weights: real bindings'), a 221 wpm turn into the story, and a punchline ('Nobody told it to plan') that the music half-buries.
dimensionNotes.story: The case-file frame pays off almost every plant: the dinner bet, Widrow's lantern, the dark lantern, and a finale that bookends the opening cursor with a match struck on 'candles'. It loses ground where the present-day stretch (ch15 s01-s05) reads like a news crawl, a silent Hassabis beat interrupts the holdouts' reunion, and the last stamp seems to reopen a question the film just answered.
dimensionNotes.visual: The silhouette and paper-cut look is consistent and often striking, such as the cathedral of stencils and the all-pairs attention hall. It sits right at the bar because figures still stand like identical mannequins, sets are bare next to the reference, and a few frames read as placeholders or double exposures (blank chip backs, a translucent candle shelf, a black blob mid-truck).
dimensionNotes.sync: Picture lands on the spoken word almost everywhere: threads fan on 'every', the flame catches on 'candles', the tower stacks on 'deep'. What remains: a Hassabis caption and pinning hand play in silence before the next line, and a few cards stay readable a beat too long or too briefly.
dimensionNotes.sound: The mix is clean (-16 LUFS, every line within 2 dB of the median) and the ending is scored precisely to picture. It is the one dimension below the bar: 'Nobody told it to plan' is masked by the score's low floor (8.6 dB margin), the turn into the story is rushed at 221 wpm, and two of the three STATUS: OPEN stamps are silent.
dimensionNotes.curiosity: The film opens with a riddle ('who taught it?') and keeps adding open questions (who paid for dinner, can a fence hold, how far and how fast) that pull a viewer through 36 minutes. It closes on an honest open file rather than a verdict.
